description:
Found while correcting cluster.md for bedrock-5tq.4.

`Bedrock.Cluster.capability/0` (lib/bedrock/cluster.ex:23) is:

    :coordination | :log | :materializer | :resolution

But `children_for_capabilities/3` (lib/bedrock/internal/cluster_supervisor.ex:193-195) maps EVERY declared capability through `module_for_capability/1` (:251-255), which handles only `:coordination`, `:materializer` and `:log` and otherwise raises `"Unknown capability: ..."`.

## Failure scenario

A node configured per the type — `capabilities: [:coordination, :materializer, :log, :resolution]` — raises at supervisor start and never boots. The guide documented exactly that configuration, which is how this surfaced.

`:resolution` is not meaningless: the Coordinator derives it (coordinator/state.ex:187 maps `:resolution` to the coordination nodes) so resolvers are PLACED on coordination nodes rather than advertised by a node. So the atom belongs to the derived capability map, not to the node-advertised list — but the type does not distinguish the two.

## Fix

Decide which it is and make the type say so. Either narrow `Cluster.capability/0` to the three a node may advertise and give the coordinator's derived map its own type, or teach `module_for_capability/1` that `:resolution` contributes no children. The current state lets the type invite a configuration the supervisor rejects.

## Test (write first, must fail)

Start a cluster supervisor with `:resolution` among the capabilities and assert it either boots or returns a clear configuration error — not a raise from a catch-all clause.
title: [BUG] Cluster.capability/0 permits :resolution but starting a node with it raises
